channel.title: The Picky Reader — New Releases
channel.description: New and notable theology releases, tracked weekly.

item.title: A Covenant Feast — J. Ryan Davidson
item.description: Recovering a richer, more biblical vision of the Lord's Supper as a true means of grace.

item.title: Apocrypha and the Septuagint — Bruce W. Longenecker, Marieke Dhont & James K. Aitken
item.description: A scholarly introduction to the Apocrypha and the Greek Old Testament. Releases 8/11.

item.title: Interpreting Biblical Metaphors — Erin Heim
item.description: Biblical metaphors can be complicated and confusing. It can be tempting to read them as universal and context-free, assume they map directly onto modern life, or treat them as interchangeable with contemporary…

item.title: An Introduction to the OT — John Goldingay
item.description: Goldingay displays a robust confidence in the truthfulness of Scripture combined with a refreshing trust in the reader's ability to grapple responsibly with the Old Testament.

item.title: James Revisited — Brandon Crowe
item.description: Despite its reputation as an outlier, James resonates with the whole canon of the Bible. This letter refracts the Old Testament through Jesus's teachings in order to urge believers to maturity in the Lord.

item.title: The Four Senses of Scripture — Patrick Schreiner
item.description: For nearly 1,700 years, the church read Scripture through four interwoven lenses, literal, allegorical, tropological, and anagogical, known as the quadriga.

item.title: Exegetical Fallacies — D. A. Carson & Andrew David Naselli
item.description: D. A.

item.title: Jerusalem Calls — Tammy Priest
item.description: In Jerusalem Calls, Tammy Priest tells the remarkable story of how God drew her to himself, and opens up the three Old Testament pilgrimage feasts that shaped her Jewish childhood to reveal something she had…

item.title: Connected — Gary Edward Schnittjer
item.description: An accessible, hands-on introduction to biblical hermeneutics built around Scripture's interconnectedness.

item.title: All-Sufficient God — Martyn Lloyd Jones
item.description: These mighty sermons from Isaiah chapter 40 show that the God of the Bible is not only the great Creator and Judge but the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort who meets us at the point of our deepest need.

item.title: Gems of Thought — William Gurnall
item.description: These ‘gems of thought’ from Gurnall’s writings will serve as helpful daily prompts for meditation, and will, if read prayerfully, lead readers to set their minds on heavenly things.

item.title: Every Perfect Gift — Joseph Lanier
item.description: Balancing depth and breadth, this book provides a robust biblical, theological, and historical discussion on the role of the seven virtues in Christian formation from a uniquely evangelical perspective.

item.title: Those Things Most Surely Believed — Joey Tomlinson
item.description: Discover the timeless wisdom of the Second London Baptist Confession of Faith (1689) with Pastor Joey Tomlinson in Those Things Most Surely Believed.

item.title: Lamentations — Mark J. Boda
item.description: The book of Lamentations is disturbing, says highly regarded Old Testament scholar Mark J. Boda.

item.title: A Godward Life — John Piper
item.description: A Godward Life features 120 meditations by John Piper that focus on the radical difference it makes when we choose to live with God at the center of all that we do.

item.title: Old Testament Wisdom Literature and Spiritual Formation — Brittany N. Melton
item.description: This volume offers insights regarding how Old Testament wisdom literature, specifically its proverbs and aphoristic material, was and can be used for spiritual formation.

item.title: Taking Back Truth — Douglas Groothuis
item.description: With a strong desire to help readers discern truth from error, senior apologist Douglas Groothuis explores our culture's deficient view of truth and clearly explains the nature of truth, how to know if something…

item.title: Taste and See — John Piper
item.description: Taste and See features 125 meditations by John Piper that awaken spiritual hunger, address life's most difficult questions, and nourish hearts with God's satisfying grace.

item.title: Dead to Sin, Alive to God in Christ — Klyne R. Snodgrass
item.description: In this exposition of Romans 6, two senior scholars offer guidance on preaching and teaching major Pauline theological concepts.

item.title: Reading the Later New Testament as Christian Scripture — Ruth Anne Reese & Madison N. Pierce
item.description: A literary, canonical, and theological introduction to Hebrews through Revelation.

item.title: Theological Foundations for Counseling — J. V. Fesko
item.description: Fesko charts a course beyond the biblical-versus-integrationist debate, grounded in the rich soil of classic Reformed theology.

item.title: Pastoral Mentoring — Jared Wilson
item.description: In Pastoral Mentoring: For the Care of Souls, Jared Wilson argues that, while formal theological education plays an important role, the local church is uniquely equipped to train its shepherds.

item.title: Knowing Christianity: The Foundations of the Christian Faith and How They Shape Daily Life — J. I. Packer · foreword by Gavin Ortlund
item.description: A new edition of Packer's accessible primer on the essentials of the faith.

item.title: Candles in the Darkness: Experiencing Advent with the Early and Medieval Church — Lynneth Miller Renberg & Adam R. Renberg
item.description: An Advent devotional drawing on the early and medieval church — plan ahead for the season.

item.title: Understanding John Wesley — Roger William Fay
item.description: Understanding John Wesley offers a compelling, accessible exploration of one of Christianity's most influential leaders.

item.title: The Path to Being a Missionary — Ryan Robertson & Matt Bennett
item.description: In The Path to Being a Missionary, Ryan Robertson and Matt Bennett help readers honestly evaluate their character, convictions, and competencies to determine if missionary work is the right fit…

item.title: Bringing the Gospel to the Nations — Iain M. Duguid
item.description: Following the progress of the gospel and the perseverance of the saints, Iain M. Duguid draws practical lessons from the life of the early church and encourages believers toward gospel-driven mission.

item.title: Spurgeon's Pastoral Wisdom: Articles on the Church and the Ministry from The Sword and the Trowel — Compiled & edited by Geoffrey Chang · C. H. Spurgeon
item.description: Spurgeon's convictions on church structure and the trials of pastoral ministry, gathered from The Sword and the Trowel.

item.title: The Apostles' Creed — Franklin Ferreira
item.description: Professor Franklin Ferreira offers a doctrinal and practical study of the Apostles' Creed that affirms the essential doctrines of the Christian faith.

item.title: 1 Kings For You — Tim Chester
item.description: An accessible expository walk through 1 Kings, pointing to the true and better King.
